expectations.text: Includes a risk register or ranking that scores the core areas (account linking, holdings, transactions, performance/returns) by risk, not just a flat feature list
expectations.evidence: Section 3, 'Risk-Based Prioritization' table ranks 11 items by Likelihood x Impact into High/Medium/Low tiers with rationale, and explicitly checks its own distribution ('5 of 11 items (~45%) are High...').

expectations.text: Manual test cases use a structured, executable format (ID, preconditions, steps, expected result) rather than prose descriptions
expectations.evidence: 38 test cases (TC-LINK-01 through TC-A11Y-02) each formatted as ID/Title/Priority/Preconditions/Steps/Expected Result/Test Data code blocks.

expectations.text: Identifies account linking / authentication as a high-risk area given it involves financial credentials
expectations.evidence: Risk table row #1 ranks 'Account linking' High, and Section B is a dedicated 'Security & Session Isolation (High Risk)' group with 5 cases.

expectations.text: Identifies performance/returns calculation as a high-risk area given numerical correctness matters for financial data
expectations.evidence: Risk table row #2 ranks 'Performance & returns calculations' High ('Silent calculation errors are the single most damaging bug class...'); Section E has 7 dedicated cases including hand-calculated verification (TC-PERF-01, 02).

expectations.text: Defines entry and/or exit criteria for the test effort, not just a list of test cases
expectations.evidence: Section 4 'Entry & Exit Criteria' lists 4 entry conditions and 6 exit conditions including waiver rules for financial calculation cases.

expectations.text: Includes negative or edge-case test cases (not only happy-path scenarios)
expectations.evidence: TC-LINK-04/05/06 (invalid creds, outage, network loss), TC-HOLD-04/05/06 (zero positions, large volume, fractional shares), TC-PERF-06/07 (no history, flat performance) are all explicit negative/edge cases.

eval_feedback.overall: This eval is not discriminating on its own -- the without_skill baseline also passes all 6 assertions with comparable structure and depth, because a well-known domain (risk-based test strategy for a fintech app) is within general model knowledge. The differentiator here isn't presence/absence of these elements but process rigor: with_skill explicitly labels its work as 'Phase 0'/'Phase 1', maintains a live deliverables checklist, and proactively calls out that Gate 1 (peer review) is unmet and blocks progression -- none of which the baseline does since it has no concept of gates. Consider adding an assertion that checks for this gate-awareness/checklist behavior specifically, since that's the actual skill-specific value being tested here.
